test.title: Cornell Admissions - Standardized Testing Policy and English Language Proficiency

aid.title: Cornell Financial Aid - First-Year and Transfer Students, International

test_policy.notes: First-year applicants must submit SAT or ACT scores (science section of ACT not required). Self-reporting allowed; official scores required on enrollment.

requirements.notes: Cornell supplement includes essays specific to the college/school applied to. International applicants seeking Cornell grant aid must file the CSS Profile when they apply. The deadlines page shows month/day only (no year).

deadlines.label: Early Decision (binding)
deadlines.notes: Application, fee/waiver and any portfolio or design supplement due Nov 1; all other required materials due Nov 13. Decisions mid-December (no exact date published).

deadlines.label: Regular Decision
deadlines.notes: Application, fee/waiver and any portfolio or design supplement due Jan 2; all other required materials due Jan 19. Decisions late March (no exact date published).

deadlines.label: International aid application (ED)
deadlines.notes: Deadline for international students; missing it forfeits aid eligibility for the whole undergraduate career.

deadlines.label: International aid application (RD)
deadlines.notes: Deadline for international students; missing it forfeits aid eligibility for the whole undergraduate career.

english_policy.waiver_notes: No exam needed if English is your native language or English has been the primary language of instruction for the past four years. Scores can be self-reported on the Common App; official scores required on enrollment.

english.notes: Exams taken before January 2026. Cornell lists these as the scores to be most competitive.
Exams taken January 2026 or later (1-6 scale): minimum 5.0, recommended 5.5.

aid.notes: International admission is need-aware. Cornell meets 100% of admitted international undergraduates' demonstrated need (grants, work-study and student loans). Apply for aid at the time of admission application with the CSS Profile (code 2098).

tier_notes.computer_science: Top-10 CS program; just outside the top-5 group.
tier_notes.business: Dyson (applied economics & management) and Nolan (hotel administration) are top-15 undergraduate business programs.
tier_notes.biology_life_sci: Top-10 life sciences (very strong in agriculture and ecology).
tier_notes.pre_med: Strong pre-med outcomes and research access; Weill Cornell Medicine affiliation.
tier_notes.arts_design: College of Architecture, Art and Planning has a top-ranked undergraduate architecture program.
